Daniel Pienaar School (Rally Rookies)

By: Floris Kotze | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Not your average school, we travel to the Eastern Cape to see what sets this school apart...

Unique Selling Point:
The only school in South Africa that offers motorsport as a subject! It is a unique look into what it takes to run a programme like this for the boys and girls from Kariega.

Summary:
The small town of Kariega (formerly Uitenhage), about 25 km north of Port Elizabeth, is not only famous for being home to the oldest technical school in South Africa, Daniel Pienaar Technical High school, but is also renowned for its big sporting achievements having been the training ground for world class sportsmen like Chassen Bright, Heino Bezuidenhout, Daniel Saayman (professional rugby in France), Dewald Potgieter, Nantie Hayward and Wernich Van Rensburg. What not everyone may realise however that it is also probably the only school in South Africa with motorsport as an official school sport. With customised cars and the sound of roaring engines, pupils at Daniel Pienaar Technical High School are living every boy’s dream at the only known school locally — and one of only three in the world — to offer motorsport as an extra-curricular activity. The school even boasts its very own 4km racing circuit alongside a professional rally team and are making some impressive headway here too. Francois Vermaak, who heads up motorsport at the school says, motorsport at school level has an impact as three of DP’s former learners are now navigating at professional level.- **Global Rarity:** One of just three schools worldwide providing motorsport as an extra-curricular activity. Educating students on vehicles and engines. **Empowering Women:** Matric student Ashley Pape advancing in timekeeping, fostering gender equality in motorsport. “Our school curriculum also complements our motorsport. Our students refer to it as ‘Motor’ and it forms one of the streams in our Mechanical Technology Department. “Learners, under the very capable guidance of well-qualified, highly experienced teachers, learn about components of a vehicle, as well as the servicing of engines. They are exposed to diagnostic systems to remain abreast with developments in the motor industry. This subject comprises theoretical and practical components and Mr Paul Ludeke, an enthusiastic Automotive teacher at our school, gleans international experience by rendering his services as a mechanic at the Dakar Rallies. He shares his knowledge and experience with our learners and colleagues, and this is of immeasurable value. DP learners and teachers are thus very involved in the various facets of Motorsport,” says Headmistress Kola du Toit.*VW Support:** Volkswagen sponsorship includes a VW Polo 1.2 tsi Rally car and a 1.4i Citi Golf rally car.- **MSA's Continuous Support:** The school appreciates Motorsport South Africa's unwavering backing beyond motorsport achievements.

Extra Budget Items:
Travel - flight to PE and Return. Car rental too.

Script:


Opening:
Drone over Uitenhage

Cut to house:
“Ash, what time are you writing today? I'm starting at 9.”

Ashley Papé:
“My name is Ashley Papé. I am nearly 18 years old. And my interests are quite different to other girls my age... And it's not just because I have my own bike.”

Opening Link:
This is Daniel Pienaar Technical High School in the Eastern Cape. We're not here to report on crime and corruption. This is an inspirational story, playing itself out in Kariega, formerly known as Uitenhage, a town with motoring running through its veins.

Ms Kola Du Toit
It's the oldest technical school in the country, it's 128 years old. And then apart from being the oldest one, we are special when it comes to something like motorsport. We're the only school in the country with motorsport as a sport.

VO 1:
That's right... Unlike most schools, students here are encouraged to speed through the school parking lot in their kitted out cars. And principal Kola du Toit is one of the first to cheer them on when they take part in regional showdowns.

Ms Kola Du Toit
If our children hear engines, then immediately they stop concentrating on everything else.
Because motor mechanics, it's one of our subjects, the sport actually fits the school like a glove. In Grade 8 they start in the pits, and then it will depend on the child's interest.(...) The kid must have a learners and then they test them on the roads and they look at maturity,(...) willingness to work as well because you don't just drive and get out and look smart, you're part of the team there.

LINK:
Daniel Pienaar Technical High School is one of only three schools in the world where motorsport is offered as an official sport, but it's about so much more than just racing fast cars.

Ashley Papé:
“Easy tiger”
I was just going through the different sports that we can, you know, pick for what you'd like to do and my mum and I were going through it and she looked at motorsport and she said I think you'd like this, try it out.


VO 2:
Joining the school's Motorsport program has been a blast for Ashley Papé! Apart from tinkering with cars, she earns money as a timekeeper at big race events.

Ashley:
It's not in the norm for a girl to be able to do this and being a girl and coming so far and it's amazing and I think it's definitely something that other girls can look at and go, if you've gotten interested in, go for it.
I definitely owe a big thanks to Mr. Vermaak for being involved in all of this.

Upsound:
“We have to put Petrol in the Golf…”

Teachers:
We two are the teachers at this school, we are also the motor teachers at this school and obviously it makes quite a lot of sense being involved in motorsport. So we are actually partners in the radical under the flag of Daniel Pienaar.

VO 3:
Francois Vermaak and Paul Ludeke - both motoring aficionados in their own right - teach the learners everything they need to know. From fixing a bent axle to hitting the apex, both the pit crew and young drivers are in experienced hands.

Together, Paul, a Dakar Rally veteran, and Francois - an avid driver - are empowering youngsters with a need for speed as they sprint towards the podium and a promising future.

Teachers:
Paul
For the motorsport kids, a lot of them see you in another light. They see opportunity for themselves because I always told them that you don't need to to be a academical achiever, you need to work with your hands and we've got a saying in our workshop as well, if you can work with your hands and you want to work, that there will always be work.
Francois
Everywhere from the guy that's driving the car straight down to the person actually washing the windows, they've all got an important job.

Chassen
I know of numerous kids that are working within motorsport now today that wouldn't have been involved in motorsport if it wasn't for this project.




VO 4:
Chassen Bright is one of those kids... With national colors and karting medals under his belt, Chassen continues in his dad, Sparky Bright's, footsteps. Sparky, together with Motorsport South Africa, established the programme more than 20 years ago. The impact it's had on the students is undeniable...

Chassen
Motorsports South Africa brought a lot of this to the school where they've supported with a lot of features that help grow the sport especially when it comes to diversity. This is one of the most important things that the project was started for was that we could take it to the people that would not normally see it. We can show people it's not only about the money you can be as poor as anyone is and still be able to be a part of motorsport in some kind of asset even if it's not driving.

VOXIES:


One day when I go out of the school when I'm matriculate I want to be a rally driver and that's what I'm going to be pursuing afterwards.

People think that girls are unable to do the work,
and that it is only for boys. But I think it is for both, boys and girls.

I would love to have a career in motorsport. I'd love to own my own car and be a driver!

VO 5:
But enough talk... It's time for me to experience the thrill of racing first-hand.

The school's top rally driver, De Villiers Wessels, was ready to take me for a quick spin.

Lourensa
​​I am so excited! I want to sit in the driver's seat!

RACE

VO6: Fortunately, no one was injured.

Link
So we came around these corners at quite a speed and as we rounded this corner we were getting ready to go down the straight and the driver unfortunately hit the curb. As you can see there's a little bit of damage.



Teachers
Sometimes the only way that they'll learn, learn from your own mistakes and you've got to make mistakes. That's why we oversee them and if they make a mistake then you just help them with that.
If you see when they get here they are scared of touching the tools and when they leave here they are hands-on.(...)

It's not about how hard you fall in love, it's about how quickly you can get up and face life again and go forward with it.

Francois:
There was a lot of times that a lack of funding was the possibility that the program would completely close down and luckily a lot of people stepped forward and started helping.

VO 7:
The programme has grown in popularity ever since the first tyre hit the tarmac nearly two decades ago. So much so that the school is looking to add a third car to its fleet...

Upsounds
So now he knows that I want to drive next year, and he messes up the car!
At least I'll help to fix it!

Talking to Lourensa
Here is a little gift for you...Nowhere on the pacenotes does it mention the curb...Will you be able to use this again? No ma'am, it is broken. It's kaput.

Closing Link:
After spending time with the kids it's clear that they are not afraid of getting their hands dirty. The school has truly created something powerful, a platform for the kids to follow their dreams.


Ms Kola
I think even if you yourself know nothing about motorsport you must understand that if the child is interested in it and you can feel that passion that could become the livelihood and the world of that child and allow him or her to look after a family one time.

Ashleigh
Motorsports, it's in my life now and I don't ever want to get rid of it. I feel like my passion for that will never go away.
I think I'm going to enjoy that for the rest of my life.



PROMOS
1x21
It's South Africa's motoring mecca, home to one of the country's favourite vehicle manufacturers. But Kariega in the Eastern Cape has another hidden gem that you probably didn't even know about.
Francois:
Not all kids are good rugby or cricket players.(...) This is exactly the type of thing that they need.

21”
ASHLEY: Just to go work on a car , its fun….
Lourensa:
At Daniel Pienaar Technical High School, motorsport is more than just a sport.
Join me for an adrenaline-filled ride.
3x21” VO
Ash
We are the only school in South Africa that offers motorsport as a sport, one of three in the world, so it's amazing.
VO:
ASHLEY: It is amazing working on cars.
VO: Fast cars, dirt roads and a passion for racing… ordinarily you wouldn’t associate this with a school…
But this school in the Eastern Cape is helping students leave the classroom in the dust!

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Not your average school, we travel to the Eastern Cape to see what sets this school apart...
metadata.Unique Selling Point: The only school in South Africa that offers motorsport as a subject! It is a unique look into what it takes to run a programme like this for the boys and girls from Kariega.
metadata.Summary: The small town of Kariega (formerly Uitenhage), about 25 km north of Port Elizabeth, is not only famous for being home to the oldest technical school in South Africa, Daniel Pienaar Technical High school, but is also renowned for its big sporting achievements having been the training ground for world class sportsmen like Chassen Bright, Heino Bezuidenhout, Daniel Saayman (professional rugby in France), Dewald Potgieter, Nantie Hayward and Wernich Van Rensburg. What not everyone may realise however that it is also probably the only school in South Africa with motorsport as an official school sport. With customised cars and the sound of roaring engines, pupils at Daniel Pienaar Technical High School are living every boy’s dream at the only known school locally — and one of only three in the world — to offer motorsport as an extra-curricular activity. The school even boasts its very own 4km racing circuit alongside a professional rally team and are making some impressive headway here too. Francois Vermaak, who heads up motorsport at the school says, motorsport at school level has an impact as three of DP’s former learners are now navigating at professional level.- **Global Rarity:** One of just three schools worldwide providing motorsport as an extra-curricular activity. Educating students on vehicles and engines. **Empowering Women:** Matric student Ashley Pape advancing in timekeeping, fostering gender equality in motorsport. “Our school curriculum also complements our motorsport. Our students refer to it as ‘Motor’ and it forms one of the streams in our Mechanical Technology Department. “Learners, under the very capable guidance of well-qualified, highly experienced teachers, learn about components of a vehicle, as well as the servicing of engines. They are exposed to diagnostic systems to remain abreast with developments in the motor industry. This subject comprises theoretical and practical components and Mr Paul Ludeke, an enthusiastic Automotive teacher at our school, gleans international experience by rendering his services as a mechanic at the Dakar Rallies. He shares his knowledge and experience with our learners and colleagues, and this is of immeasurable value. DP learners and teachers are thus very involved in the various facets of Motorsport,” says Headmistress Kola du Toit.*VW Support:** Volkswagen sponsorship includes a VW Polo 1.2 tsi Rally car and a 1.4i Citi Golf rally car.- **MSA's Continuous Support:** The school appreciates Motorsport South Africa's unwavering backing beyond motorsport achievements.
